To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

import competition affects the level of employment by influencing the rate of plant startup/shutdown and by inducing changes in product mix across industries, but does not affect the level of employment at plants continuously operating within an industry.

job creation by new plants and job creation by plants that alter their product mix are sensitive to import competition, while job destruction at plants that alter their products and job creation at plants that do not alter their products are not sensitive to import competition.
(1) job flows at plants entering or exiting the market are responsive to import competition, and (2) job flows at existing plants within the same industries are not responsive to import competition.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of import competition on employment in the manufacturing sector.
the relationship between import price and employment in Japan, and we have shown that import competition has a significant impact on employment in the Japanese manufacturing industry.
how import competition affects the structure of the Japanese economy, as well as the employment consequences of import competition.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
import competition has had a strong impact on job creation/destruction, especially through plant startups/shutdown, but not on job flows at plants operating within the same industry.
the Japanese economy was more flexible in terms of plant startups and shutdowns and less flexible in terms of product changes.
import price changes had a significant effect on the creation and destruction of jobs in Japan.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
import competition was a major factor in employment adjustment during the Bubble boom, and that the effects on employment were not uniform across plants.
employment in Japanese manufacturing is more flexible to import competition than has previously been thought.
the effects of import competition on employment in Japan during the Bubble period were more pronounced at the industry and product level than at the firm level.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effects of import competition on employment are not limited to job destruction at plants that shut down.
the impact of import competition on employment is highly heterogeneous, and the effects depend on the nature of the job flows and the industry in which the plants operate.
import competition has a large and significant impact on the employment adjustment process.
